claim: Malaria killed 429,000 people worldwide in 2016, about 70% of whom were African children under 5 years of age.
source: the WHO Malaria Report estimated that malaria killed 429,000 people worldwide in 2016, about 70% of whom were African children under 5 years of age (World Malaria Report 2016).
evidence: The claim cites the WHO Malaria Report 2016 as the source of the mortality statistics.

claim: Orange vessels on clinical examination are strongly associated with death in children with P. falciparum cerebral malaria (OR 2.90, 95% CI: 1.96–4.30, p<0.001).
source: Orange vessels and severe foveal whitening (clinical examination, n = 817, OR, 95% CI: 2.90, 1.96–4.30; 3.4, 1.8–6.3, both p<0.001), and arteriolar involvement by intravascular filling defects (angiographic image analysis, n = 260, 2.81, 1.17–6.72, p<0.02) were strongly associated with death.
evidence: The claim is supported by statistical analysis of clinical examination data from 817 subjects showing odds ratios and confidence intervals.

claim: Severe foveal whitening is strongly associated with death in children with P. falciparum cerebral malaria (OR 3.4, 95% CI: 1.8–6.3, p<0.001).
source: Orange vessels and severe foveal whitening (clinical examination, n = 817, OR, 95% CI: 2.90, 1.96–4.30; 3.4, 1.8–6.3, both p<0.001), and arteriolar involvement by intravascular filling defects (angiographic image analysis, n = 260, 2.81, 1.17–6.72, p<0.02) were strongly associated with death.
evidence: The claim is supported by statistical analysis of clinical examination data from 817 subjects showing odds ratios and confidence intervals.

claim: Arteriolar involvement by intravascular filling defects is strongly associated with death (OR 2.81, 95% CI: 1.17–6.72, p<0.02).
source: Orange vessels and severe foveal whitening (clinical examination, n = 817, OR, 95% CI: 2.90, 1.96–4.30; 3.4, 1.8–6.3, both p<0.001), and arteriolar involvement by intravascular filling defects (angiographic image analysis, n = 260, 2.81, 1.17–6.72, p<0.02) were strongly associated with death.
evidence: The claim is supported by angiographic image analysis data from 260 subjects showing odds ratios and confidence intervals.

claim: Orange vessels contain dense sequestration of late stage parasitised red cells with sensitivity 0.97 and specificity 0.89.
source: Orange vessels had dense sequestration of late stage parasitised red cells (histopathology, n = 29; sensitivity 0.97, specificity 0.89) involving 360° of the lumen circumference, with altered protein expression in blood-retinal barrier cells and marked loss/disruption of pericytes.
evidence: The claim is supported by histopathological analysis of 29 cases with calculated sensitivity and specificity values.

claim: Orange vessels show sequestration involving 360° of the lumen circumference.
source: Orange vessels had dense sequestration of late stage parasitised red cells (histopathology, n = 29; sensitivity 0.97, specificity 0.89) involving 360° of the lumen circumference, with altered protein expression in blood-retinal barrier cells and marked loss/disruption of pericytes.
evidence: The claim is supported by histopathological observations from 29 cases.

claim: Orange vessels show altered protein expression in blood-retinal barrier cells.
source: Orange vessels had dense sequestration of late stage parasitised red cells (histopathology, n = 29; sensitivity 0.97, specificity 0.89) involving 360° of the lumen circumference, with altered protein expression in blood-retinal barrier cells and marked loss/disruption of pericytes.
evidence: The claim is supported by histopathological analysis of 29 cases examining protein expression.

claim: Orange vessels show marked loss/disruption of pericytes.
source: Orange vessels had dense sequestration of late stage parasitised red cells (histopathology, n = 29; sensitivity 0.97, specificity 0.89) involving 360° of the lumen circumference, with altered protein expression in blood-retinal barrier cells and marked loss/disruption of pericytes.
evidence: The claim is supported by histopathological analysis of 29 cases examining pericyte structure.

claim: Retinal whitening is topographically associated with tissue response to hypoxia.
source: Retinal whitening was topographically associated with tissue response to hypoxia.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry analysis showing increased VEGFR1 and AQP4 expression in areas of whitening.

claim: Sequestration of parasitised red blood cells in the cerebral neurovasculature is the key underlying pathophysiological feature in P. falciparum CM.
source: Sequestration of parasitised red blood cells (pRBC) in the cerebral neurovasculature is the key underlying pathophysiological feature in P. falciparum CM (Turner, 1997).
evidence: The claim cites Turner, 1997 as the source for this established pathophysiological mechanism.

claim: The degree and location of neurovascular abnormalities can be observed clinically in the retina using routinely available ophthalmological techniques.
source: Unlike in the brain, the degree and location of neurovascular abnormalities can be observed clinically in the retina using routinely available ophthalmological techniques (Harding et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim cites Harding et al., 2006 and is supported by the clinical examination methods described in the study.

claim: Malarial retinopathy features comprise orange or white retinal vessels, patchy or confluent retinal whitening and white centred retinal haemorrhages.
source: Features comprise orange or white retinal vessels, patchy or confluent retinal whitening and white centred retinal haemorrhages (Figure 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by clinical observations and illustrated in Figure 1.

claim: Severity of MR predicts the risk of death and duration of coma.
source: Severity of MR predicts the risk of death and duration of coma (Beare et al., 2004; Lewallen et al., 2008; Beare et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim cites three studies (Beare et al., 2004; Lewallen et al., 2008; Beare et al., 2006) that established this association.

claim: Subjects who did not have an admission retinal exam were likely to have a higher serum lactate concentration (p<0.001).
source: Subjects who did not have an admission retinal exam were likely to have a higher serum lactate concentration (p<0.001) and were more likely to die (p<0.006).
evidence: The claim is supported by statistical comparison of subjects with and without retinal examination.

claim: Subjects who did not have an admission retinal exam were more likely to die (p<0.006).
source: Subjects who did not have an admission retinal exam were likely to have a higher serum lactate concentration (p<0.001) and were more likely to die (p<0.006).
evidence: The claim is supported by statistical comparison of subjects with and without retinal examination.

claim: Subjects who did not have an admission retinal exam were, on average, 5 months younger (p<0.001) than those who had retinal examinations.
source: They were, on average, 5 months younger (p<0.001) and 0.2 kg lighter (p<0.01) than those who had retinal examinations.
evidence: The claim is supported by statistical comparison of demographic characteristics between groups.

claim: Subjects who did not have an admission retinal exam were 0.2 kg lighter (p<0.01) than those who had retinal examinations.
source: They were, on average, 5 months younger (p<0.001) and 0.2 kg lighter (p<0.01) than those who had retinal examinations.
evidence: The claim is supported by statistical comparison of demographic characteristics between groups.

claim: Of 817 subjects with retinopathy-positive CM, 137 (16.8%) died.
source: On admission, 817 subjects had retinopathy-positive CM. Of these, 137 (16.8%) died with the time from admission to death less than 24 hr for the majority.
evidence: The claim reports mortality data from the clinical dataset.

claim: The time from admission to death was less than 24 hr for the majority of deaths.
source: On admission, 817 subjects had retinopathy-positive CM. Of these, 137 (16.8%) died with the time from admission to death less than 24 hr for the majority.
evidence: The claim reports temporal data on mortality from the clinical dataset.

claim: Papilloedema was more likely in those who died (OR 2.29, 95% CI 1.55–3.38, p<0.001).
source: Papilloedema (odds ratio (OR) 2.29, 95% confidence interval 1.55–3.38, p<0.001) and disc hyperaemia (OR 1.73, 1.15–2.62, p<0.01), both indicators of brain swelling, were more likely in those who died.
evidence: The claim is supported by statistical analysis from Table 1 showing odds ratios and confidence intervals.

claim: Disc hyperaemia was more likely in those who died (OR 1.73, 95% CI 1.15–2.62, p<0.01).
source: Papilloedema (odds ratio (OR) 2.29, 95% confidence interval 1.55–3.38, p<0.001) and disc hyperaemia (OR 1.73, 1.15–2.62, p<0.01), both indicators of brain swelling, were more likely in those who died.
evidence: The claim is supported by statistical analysis from Table 1 showing odds ratios and confidence intervals.

claim: Papilloedema and disc hyperaemia are both indicators of brain swelling.
source: Papilloedema (odds ratio (OR) 2.29, 95% confidence interval 1.55–3.38, p<0.001) and disc hyperaemia (OR 1.73, 1.15–2.62, p<0.01), both indicators of brain swelling, were more likely in those who died.
evidence: The claim draws on established medical knowledge about the clinical significance of these ophthalmic findings.

claim: In multivariable regression analysis adjusting for confounders, orange vessels remained significantly associated with death (OR 2.85, 95% CI 1.72–4.74, p<0.001, n = 549).
source: When including potential confounders (age, WCC, HRP2, lactate, papilloedema - see Materials and methods) in a multivariable regression model for the presence of the two retinal features with death, we found similar ORs and significance (orange vessels: OR 2.85, 1.72–4.74, p<0.001, n = 549; foveal whitening: OR 3.57, 1.57–8.13, p=0.002, n = 615).
evidence: The claim is supported by multivariable statistical analysis controlling for potential confounders.

claim: In multivariable regression analysis adjusting for confounders, foveal whitening remained significantly associated with death (OR 3.57, 95% CI 1.57–8.13, p=0.002, n = 615).
source: When including potential confounders (age, WCC, HRP2, lactate, papilloedema - see Materials and methods) in a multivariable regression model for the presence of the two retinal features with death, we found similar ORs and significance (orange vessels: OR 2.85, 1.72–4.74, p<0.001, n = 549; foveal whitening: OR 3.57, 1.57–8.13, p=0.002, n = 615).
evidence: The claim is supported by multivariable statistical analysis controlling for potential confounders.

claim: All orange vessels exhibited pigmented pRBCs sequestered in layers on the endothelium at the margin of the vessel lumen, with a blood column consisting of uninfected RBCs in the centre of affected vessels.
source: All orange vessels exhibited pigmented pRBCs sequestered in layers on the endothelium at the margin of the vessel lumen, with a blood column consisting of uninfected RBCs in the centre of affected vessels (Figure 2C, Figure 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by histopathological examination of orange vessels from 12 cases with 212 vessels analyzed.

claim: White vessels (usually distended capillaries) contained primarily extraerythrocytic haemozoin (HZ) and some remnants of pRBC; non-parasitised RBCs were absent.
source: White vessels (usually distended capillaries) contained primarily extraerythrocytic haemozoin (HZ) and some remnants of pRBC; non-parasitised RBCs were absent.
evidence: The claim is supported by histopathological examination of white vessels.

claim: Fibrin polymers were detected in retinal capillaries and venules.
source: Fibrin polymers were detected in retinal capillaries and venules (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by histopathological examination with fibrinogen immunohistochemistry.

claim: Vessels with sequestered late stage pRBCs involving 360° of the circumference of the vessel lumen were strongly associated with the presence of orange discoloration.
source: Vessels with sequestered late stage pRBCs involving 360° of the circumference of the vessel lumen were strongly associated with the presence of orange discoloration (Table 4).
evidence: The claim is supported by analysis of 412 vessels from nine MR-positive cases as shown in Table 4.

claim: Sensitivity for orange discolouration as an indicator of 360° sequestration was 0.97 (95% confidence interval: 0.94 to 0.99).
source: Sensitivity and specificity for orange discolouration as an indicator of this extent of sequestration were 0.97 (95% confidence interval: 0.94 to 0.99) and 0.89 (0.84 to 0.93), respectively, with positive and negative predictive values of 0.88 (0.83 to 0.92) and 0.98 (0.94 to 0.99).
evidence: The claim is supported by diagnostic test accuracy analysis of 412 vessels.

claim: Specificity for orange discolouration as an indicator of 360° sequestration was 0.89 (95% confidence interval: 0.84 to 0.93).
source: Sensitivity and specificity for orange discolouration as an indicator of this extent of sequestration were 0.97 (95% confidence interval: 0.94 to 0.99) and 0.89 (0.84 to 0.93), respectively, with positive and negative predictive values of 0.88 (0.83 to 0.92) and 0.98 (0.94 to 0.99).
evidence: The claim is supported by diagnostic test accuracy analysis of 412 vessels.

claim: Positive predictive value for orange discolouration as an indicator of 360° sequestration was 0.88 (95% confidence interval: 0.83 to 0.92).
source: Sensitivity and specificity for orange discolouration as an indicator of this extent of sequestration were 0.97 (95% confidence interval: 0.94 to 0.99) and 0.89 (0.84 to 0.93), respectively, with positive and negative predictive values of 0.88 (0.83 to 0.92) and 0.98 (0.94 to 0.99).
evidence: The claim is supported by diagnostic test accuracy analysis of 412 vessels.

claim: Negative predictive value for orange discolouration as an indicator of 360° sequestration was 0.98 (95% confidence interval: 0.94 to 0.99).
source: Sensitivity and specificity for orange discolouration as an indicator of this extent of sequestration were 0.97 (95% confidence interval: 0.94 to 0.99) and 0.89 (0.84 to 0.93), respectively, with positive and negative predictive values of 0.88 (0.83 to 0.92) and 0.98 (0.94 to 0.99).
evidence: The claim is supported by diagnostic test accuracy analysis of 412 vessels.

claim: Intraretinal sequestration was significantly associated with reduced expression of CD34 in retinal microvessels (p<0.005).
source: In both Grades 1 and 2 MR-positive cases, intraretinal sequestration was significantly associated with reduced expression in retinal microvessels of the endothelial cell membrane glycoprotein CD34, the pericyte structural protein smooth muscle actin (SMA) and the signalling molecule platelet derived growth factor receptor β (PDGFRβ) (Figure 4, all p<0.005)
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry analysis comparing vessels with and without sequestration.

claim: Intraretinal sequestration was significantly associated with reduced expression of smooth muscle actin (SMA) in retinal microvessels (p<0.005).
source: In both Grades 1 and 2 MR-positive cases, intraretinal sequestration was significantly associated with reduced expression in retinal microvessels of the endothelial cell membrane glycoprotein CD34, the pericyte structural protein smooth muscle actin (SMA) and the signalling molecule platelet derived growth factor receptor β (PDGFRβ) (Figure 4, all p<0.005)
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry analysis comparing vessels with and without sequestration.

claim: Intraretinal sequestration was significantly associated with reduced expression of platelet derived growth factor receptor β (PDGFRβ) in retinal microvessels (p<0.005).
source: In both Grades 1 and 2 MR-positive cases, intraretinal sequestration was significantly associated with reduced expression in retinal microvessels of the endothelial cell membrane glycoprotein CD34, the pericyte structural protein smooth muscle actin (SMA) and the signalling molecule platelet derived growth factor receptor β (PDGFRβ) (Figure 4, all p<0.005)
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry analysis comparing vessels with and without sequestration.

claim: The proportion of continuous CD34 immunostaining in capillaries and venules with pRBC sequestration was 14 ± 9%.
source: The proportions of continuous immunostaining in capillaries and venules, with and without pRBC sequestration, respectively (means ±SD), were: CD34, 14 ± 9% and 90 ± 10%; SMA 11 ± 10% and 65 ± 25%; PDGFRβ 19 ± 15% and 77 ± 18% (all p<0.005).
evidence: The claim reports quantitative immunohistochemistry data from vessel analysis.

claim: The proportion of continuous CD34 immunostaining in capillaries and venules without pRBC sequestration was 90 ± 10%.
source: The proportions of continuous immunostaining in capillaries and venules, with and without pRBC sequestration, respectively (means ±SD), were: CD34, 14 ± 9% and 90 ± 10%; SMA 11 ± 10% and 65 ± 25%; PDGFRβ 19 ± 15% and 77 ± 18% (all p<0.005).
evidence: The claim reports quantitative immunohistochemistry data from vessel analysis.

claim: The proportion of continuous SMA immunostaining in venules with pRBC sequestration was 11 ± 10%.
source: The proportions of continuous immunostaining in capillaries and venules, with and without pRBC sequestration, respectively (means ±SD), were: CD34, 14 ± 9% and 90 ± 10%; SMA 11 ± 10% and 65 ± 25%; PDGFRβ 19 ± 15% and 77 ± 18% (all p<0.005).
evidence: The claim reports quantitative immunohistochemistry data from vessel analysis.

claim: The proportion of continuous SMA immunostaining in venules without pRBC sequestration was 65 ± 25%.
source: The proportions of continuous immunostaining in capillaries and venules, with and without pRBC sequestration, respectively (means ±SD), were: CD34, 14 ± 9% and 90 ± 10%; SMA 11 ± 10% and 65 ± 25%; PDGFRβ 19 ± 15% and 77 ± 18% (all p<0.005).
evidence: The claim reports quantitative immunohistochemistry data from vessel analysis.

claim: The proportion of continuous PDGFRβ immunostaining in vessels with pRBC sequestration was 19 ± 15%.
source: The proportions of continuous immunostaining in capillaries and venules, with and without pRBC sequestration, respectively (means ±SD), were: CD34, 14 ± 9% and 90 ± 10%; SMA 11 ± 10% and 65 ± 25%; PDGFRβ 19 ± 15% and 77 ± 18% (all p<0.005).
evidence: The claim reports quantitative immunohistochemistry data from vessel analysis.

claim: The proportion of continuous PDGFRβ immunostaining in vessels without pRBC sequestration was 77 ± 18%.
source: The proportions of continuous immunostaining in capillaries and venules, with and without pRBC sequestration, respectively (means ±SD), were: CD34, 14 ± 9% and 90 ± 10%; SMA 11 ± 10% and 65 ± 25%; PDGFRβ 19 ± 15% and 77 ± 18% (all p<0.005).
evidence: The claim reports quantitative immunohistochemistry data from vessel analysis.

claim: Reduced expression of CD34, SMA, and PDGFRβ in vessels with pRBC sequestration is consistent with marked altered cell function or loss of pericytes and endothelial cells.
source: These findings are consistent with marked altered cell function or loss of pericytes and endothelial cells of vessels with pRBC sequestration.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the immunohistochemistry data based on established knowledge of these cellular markers.

claim: Percentages of vessels with normal PDGFRβ staining were significantly less in MR-positive cases with haemorrhages (18%) than those without (39%; n = 21, p<0.05).
source: Percentages of vessels with normal PDGFRβ staining were significantly less in MR-positive cases with haemorrhages (18%) than those without (39%; n = 21, p<0.05).
evidence: The claim is supported by statistical comparison of PDGFRβ staining between cases with and without hemorrhages.

claim: Glial cells surrounding venules and capillaries affected by severe pRBC sequestration showed statistically significant increases in perivascular astrocyte ICAM-1 (p=0.003).
source: There were statistically significant increases in perivascular astrocyte intercellular adhesion molecule 1 (ICAM-1) (p=0.003) and Müller cell cytoskeletal component glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) (p=0.034), markers for early (4–12 hr) and late (after 24 hr) glial activation, respectively (Lee et al., 2000; Hiscott et al., 1984).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry analysis of glial cells in 10 of 21 MR-positive cases.

claim: Glial cells surrounding venules and capillaries affected by severe pRBC sequestration showed statistically significant increases in Müller cell GFAP (p=0.034).
source: There were statistically significant increases in perivascular astrocyte intercellular adhesion molecule 1 (ICAM-1) (p=0.003) and Müller cell cytoskeletal component glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) (p=0.034), markers for early (4–12 hr) and late (after 24 hr) glial activation, respectively (Lee et al., 2000; Hiscott et al., 1984).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry analysis of glial cells in 10 of 21 MR-positive cases.

claim: ICAM-1 is a marker for early (4–12 hr) glial activation.
source: There were statistically significant increases in perivascular astrocyte intercellular adhesion molecule 1 (ICAM-1) (p=0.003) and Müller cell cytoskeletal component glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) (p=0.034), markers for early (4–12 hr) and late (after 24 hr) glial activation, respectively (Lee et al., 2000; Hiscott et al., 1984).
evidence: The claim cites Lee et al., 2000 as the source for the temporal characteristics of ICAM-1 expression.

claim: GFAP is a marker for late (after 24 hr) glial activation.
source: There were statistically significant increases in perivascular astrocyte intercellular adhesion molecule 1 (ICAM-1) (p=0.003) and Müller cell cytoskeletal component glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) (p=0.034), markers for early (4–12 hr) and late (after 24 hr) glial activation, respectively (Lee et al., 2000; Hiscott et al., 1984).
evidence: The claim cites Hiscott et al., 1984 as the source for the temporal characteristics of GFAP expression.

claim: No MR-negative cases showed perivascular ICAM-1 or GFAP immunoreactivity.
source: No MR-negative cases showed perivascular ICAM-1 or GFAP immunoreactivity.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry analysis of MR-negative control cases.

claim: ICAM-1 tissue staining was associated with the presence of discoloured vessels (all Fisher exact tests p<0.05).
source: ICAM-1 tissue staining was also associated with the presence of discoloured vessels (Figure 5A, all Fisher exact tests p<0.05), compared with normal vessels where ICAM-1 was restricted to the endothelium (Figure 5B).
evidence: The claim is supported by statistical analysis comparing ICAM-1 staining patterns between discoloured and normal vessels.

claim: Müller cell GFAP immunoreactivity was observed in 8 of the 21 (38%) cases with MR.
source: Müller cell GFAP immunoreactivity was observed in 8 of the 21 (38%) cases with MR (Figure 5C) versus MR-negative cases (Figure 5D) where staining was restricted to the first retinal layer.
evidence: The claim reports the frequency of GFAP immunoreactivity in MR-positive cases.

claim: MR-positive cases showed increased expression of VEGFR1 immunoreactivity in both central and peripheral retina.
source: MR-positive cases showed increased expression of VEGFR1 immunoreactivity in both central and peripheral retina.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry analysis comparing MR-positive and MR-negative cases.

claim: VEGFR1 immunostaining was primarily localised in the inner retina (ganglion cell and inner nuclear cell bodies and synapses).
source: VEGFR1 immunostaining was primarily localised in the inner retina (Figure 6A,B) (ganglion cell (primarily in the macula) and inner nuclear cell bodies and synapses) and values were positively correlated with increasing severity of whitening for all these cells (Figure 6C p<0.05, p<0.001) and for macular ganglion cell layers with worse MR (Figure 6D, p<0.001).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry analysis showing the distribution of VEGFR1 expression.

claim: VEGFR1 values were positively correlated with increasing severity of whitening for ganglion cells and inner nuclear cells (p<0.05, p<0.001).
source: VEGFR1 immunostaining was primarily localised in the inner retina (Figure 6A,B) (ganglion cell (primarily in the macula) and inner nuclear cell bodies and synapses) and values were positively correlated with increasing severity of whitening for all these cells (Figure 6C p<0.05, p<0.001) and for macular ganglion cell layers with worse MR (Figure 6D, p<0.001).
evidence: The claim is supported by statistical correlation analysis between VEGFR1 expression and whitening severity.

claim: VEGFR1 levels in macular ganglion cell layers were positively correlated with worse MR (p<0.001).
source: VEGFR1 immunostaining was primarily localised in the inner retina (Figure 6A,B) (ganglion cell (primarily in the macula) and inner nuclear cell bodies and synapses) and values were positively correlated with increasing severity of whitening for all these cells (Figure 6C p<0.05, p<0.001) and for macular ganglion cell layers with worse MR (Figure 6D, p<0.001).
evidence: The claim is supported by statistical correlation analysis between VEGFR1 expression and MR severity.

claim: AQP4 expression levels were generally more intense in MR-positive cases with whitening than those without.
source: AQP4 expression levels were generally more intense in MR-positive cases with whitening (Figure 1B) than those without (Figure 7, Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry analysis comparing AQP4 expression between cases with and without whitening.

claim: High AQP4 staining levels were found in glial cells, including Műller cells, in the nerve fibre layer (NFL) and outer plexiform layer in the macula.
source: High AQP4 staining levels were found in glial cells, including Műller cells, in the nerve fibre layer (NFL) and outer plexiform layer (Chen et al., 2012) in the macula (Figure 7A,B) and temporal periphery (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry analysis showing the distribution of AQP4 expression.

claim: Densitometry analysis showed significantly higher AQP4 levels for macula and temporal periphery (ANOVA test, p<0.05 except moderate whitening).
source: Densitometry analysis showed significantly higher AQP4 levels for macula and temporal periphery (Figure 7C and Figure 7—figure supplement 1, ANOVA test, p<0.05 except moderate whitening).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative densitometry analysis with statistical testing.

claim: There were statistically significant associations between AQP4 staining pattern and MR grade.
source: There were statistically significant associations also between AQP4 staining pattern and MR grade (Figure 7D and Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by statistical analysis comparing AQP4 expression across MR severity grades.

claim: In 44% of MR-positive cases in the macula, intravascular thrombi were co-localised with retinal whitening.
source: In addition to the association found between tissue whitening, VEGFR1 and AQP4 expression levels, in 44% and 68% of MR-positive cases (macula and periphery respectively) intravascular thrombi were co-localised with retinal whitening (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–C; p<0.05 for periphery only).
evidence: The claim reports the frequency of co-localization between thrombi and whitening in the macula.

claim: In 68% of MR-positive cases in the periphery, intravascular thrombi were co-localised with retinal whitening (p<0.05).
source: In addition to the association found between tissue whitening, VEGFR1 and AQP4 expression levels, in 44% and 68% of MR-positive cases (macula and periphery respectively) intravascular thrombi were co-localised with retinal whitening (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–C; p<0.05 for periphery only).
evidence: The claim reports the frequency of co-localization between thrombi and whitening in the periphery with statistical significance.

claim: Between 2009 and 2014, 260 subjects with MR-positive CM underwent retinal FA on the day or day after admission.
source: Between 2009 and 2014, 260 subjects with MR-positive CM underwent retinal FA on the day or day after admission.
evidence: The claim reports the size and timeframe of the fluorescein angiography dataset.

claim: IVFD occurred in 80.2% of large venules.
source: IVFD occurred frequently in the retinal venules (large 80.2%, small 98.0%, post capillary 98.3%).
evidence: The claim reports the frequency of IVFD in large venules from the FA dataset.

claim: IVFD occurred in 98.0% of small venules.
source: IVFD occurred frequently in the retinal venules (large 80.2%, small 98.0%, post capillary 98.3%).
evidence: The claim reports the frequency of IVFD in small venules from the FA dataset.

claim: IVFD occurred in 98.3% of post-capillary venules.
source: IVFD occurred frequently in the retinal venules (large 80.2%, small 98.0%, post capillary 98.3%).
evidence: The claim reports the frequency of IVFD in post-capillary venules from the FA dataset.

claim: There was no association between sequestration in post-capillary venules and survival (OR 0.23, 95% CI 0.054–1.02, p=0.053).
source: There was no association between sequestration in post-capillary venules and survival (OR 0.23, 0.054–1.02, p=0.053).
evidence: The claim reports statistical analysis showing no significant association between post-capillary venule sequestration and survival.

claim: Large arteriole sequestration was significantly associated with death (OR 2.81, 95% CI 1.17–6.72, p<0.02).
source: Conversely, sequestration was infrequent in the arterioles but with significant associations with death for large arteriole sequestration (OR 2.81, 1.17–6.72, p<0.02), and non-significant association for precapillary arterioles (OR 2.47, 0.94–6.45, p=0.065) (see Table 5 and Figure 9).
evidence: The claim is supported by statistical analysis of FA data showing odds ratios and confidence intervals.

claim: Precapillary arteriole sequestration showed a non-significant association with death (OR 2.47, 95% CI 0.94–6.45, p=0.065).
source: Conversely, sequestration was infrequent in the arterioles but with significant associations with death for large arteriole sequestration (OR 2.81, 1.17–6.72, p<0.02), and non-significant association for precapillary arterioles (OR 2.47, 0.94–6.45, p=0.065) (see Table 5 and Figure 9).
evidence: The claim is supported by statistical analysis of FA data showing odds ratios and confidence intervals.

claim: Precapillary arteriole sequestration was associated with longer time to recovery of consciousness (binomial regression coefficient 0.32, 95% CI 0.094–0.55, p<0.01).
source: Similar findings were found for time to recovery of consciousness (binomial regression coefficient, 95% CI): precapillary arterioles (0.32, 0.094–0.55, p<0.01), small arterioles (0.30, 0.093–0.51, p<0.01), large arterioles (0.38, 0.076–0.68, p<0.02).
evidence: The claim is supported by binomial regression analysis of time to recovery data.

claim: Small arteriole sequestration was associated with longer time to recovery of consciousness (binomial regression coefficient 0.30, 95% CI 0.093–0.51, p<0.01).
source: Similar findings were found for time to recovery of consciousness (binomial regression coefficient, 95% CI): precapillary arterioles (0.32, 0.094–0.55, p<0.01), small arterioles (0.30, 0.093–0.51, p<0.01), large arterioles (0.38, 0.076–0.68, p<0.02).
evidence: The claim is supported by binomial regression analysis of time to recovery data.

claim: Large arteriole sequestration was associated with longer time to recovery of consciousness (binomial regression coefficient 0.38, 95% CI 0.076–0.68, p<0.02).
source: Similar findings were found for time to recovery of consciousness (binomial regression coefficient, 95% CI): precapillary arterioles (0.32, 0.094–0.55, p<0.01), small arterioles (0.30, 0.093–0.51, p<0.01), large arterioles (0.38, 0.076–0.68, p<0.02).
evidence: The claim is supported by binomial regression analysis of time to recovery data.

claim: Sequestration in the capillaries was frequently seen but was ungradeable in 62% of cases.
source: Sequestration in the capillaries was frequently seen but was ungradeable in 62% of cases.
evidence: The claim reports a limitation in the FA grading methodology for capillaries.

claim: The mean ratio of affected:unaffected vessels was 41.9% in children who died and 37.8% in survivors.
source: The mean ratio of affected:unaffected vessels was 41.9% in children who died and 37.8% in survivors.
evidence: The claim reports quantitative image analysis results from 251 eyes.

claim: The amount of IVFD in retinal vessels was higher in the patients who died, but the difference did not reach statistical significance (OR 18.05, 95% CI 0.74–211.33, p<0.08).
source: The amount of IVFD in retinal vessels was higher in the patients who died in our study, but the difference did not reach statistical significance (OR 18.05, 0.74–211.33, p<0.08).
evidence: The claim reports statistical analysis of automated vessel segmentation data showing a non-significant trend.

claim: The orange appearance of retinal vessels in comatose children with CM is caused by sequestered late-stage pRBCs.
source: The clinicopathological findings from our unique cohort provide strong evidence that the orange appearance of retinal vessels in comatose children with a clinical diagnosis of CM is caused by sequestered late-stage pRBCs.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion drawn from the clinicopathological dataset showing correlation between orange vessels and pRBC sequestration.

claim: Visible sequestration is strongly associated with death, with an increased risk when arterioles are involved.
source: Our dataset of clinical outcomes, the largest to date, and our independently graded angiographic data show that this visible sequestration is strongly associated with death, with an increased risk when arterioles are involved.
evidence: The claim summarizes findings from both the clinical dataset (n=817) and FA dataset (n=260).

claim: The tissue effects of sequestration include severe loss/disruption of pericytes.
source: The tissue effects of sequestration are widespread within the neurovascular unit, including novel findings of severe loss/disruption of pericytes.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data showing reduced SMA and PDGFRβ expression in vessels with sequestration.

claim: Retinal whitening is associated with features of cytotoxic oedema, consistent with sequestration causing ischaemia.
source: Retinal whitening, also strongly associated with death, is associated with features of cytotoxic oedema, consistent with sequestration causing ischaemia.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data showing increased VEGFR1 and AQP4 expression in areas of whitening.

claim: Orange vessels can be considered as an indication of severe sequestration.
source: We think orange vessels can be considered as an indication of severe sequestration and, as such, are clinically extremely valuable.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation based on the high sensitivity and specificity of orange vessels for 360° sequestration.

claim: Orange vessels are easily visible with indirect ophthalmoscopy after pupil dilation.
source: This severe sequestration is easily visible with indirect ophthalmoscopy after pupil dilation.
evidence: The claim is based on clinical examination methods used in the study.

claim: Retinal capillary involvement appears to be a phenomenon in CM not associated with death.
source: Retinal capillary involvement, in contrast to orange vessels, appears to be a phenomenon in CM not associated with death.
evidence: The claim is based on the lack of association between white capillaries and death in the clinical dataset.

claim: White vessels are associated with non-perfusion on FA.
source: This feature was associated with non-perfusion on FA.
evidence: The claim is based on correlation between white vessels on clinical examination and capillary non-perfusion on FA.

claim: Retinal intravascular material was seen in nearly all MR-positive cases, especially the post-capillary and small venules (98.3% and 87.9% of gradeable vessels, respectively).
source: Our large fluorescein angiography (FA) study, which extended over eight seasons, shows that the retinal intravascular material was seen in nearly all MR-positive cases, especially the post-capillary and small venules (98.3% and 87.9% of gradeable vessels, respectively).
evidence: The claim reports findings from the FA dataset of 260 subjects.

claim: The presence of intravascular material in the arterioles was much less likely (pre-capillary 58.4%, small 43.9%, large 15.3%).
source: The presence of intravascular material in the arterioles was much less likely (pre-capillary 58.4%, small 43.9%, large 15.3%).
evidence: The claim reports frequencies of arteriolar involvement from the FA dataset.

claim: Arteriolar intravascular material was associated with longer recovery times (p<0.01- < 0.02).
source: However, arteriolar intravascular material was associated with longer recovery times (p<0.01- < 0.02) and greater risk of death, with involvement of the large arterioles conferring a 2.81-fold increased risk of death.
evidence: The claim is supported by statistical analysis of time to recovery data.

claim: Involvement of the large arterioles confers a 2.81-fold increased risk of death.
source: However, arteriolar intravascular material was associated with longer recovery times (p<0.01- < 0.02) and greater risk of death, with involvement of the large arterioles conferring a 2.81-fold increased risk of death.
evidence: The claim is supported by statistical analysis from the FA dataset.

claim: The involvement of the arteriolar side can be taken as a clinical marker of severity, indicating a greater extent or load of sequestration.
source: It appears that the involvement of the arteriolar side can be taken as a clinical marker of severity, indicating a greater extent or load of sequestration.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation based on the association between arteriolar involvement and worse outcomes.

claim: Reduced expression of CD34 in endothelial cells and of SMA and PDGRFβ in pericytes indicates significant dysfunction of both cell types.
source: Reduced expression of CD34 in endothelial cells and of SMA and PDGRFβ in pericytes indicates significant dysfunction of both cell types.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the immunohistochemistry data based on established knowledge of these cellular markers.

claim: Pericytes are highly sensitive to hypoxia, especially in brain and retina where they are most abundant.
source: Pericytes are highly sensitive to hypoxia (Kamouchi et al., 2012), especially in brain and retina where they are most abundant, and when vessels lose or develop abnormal pericytes they become hyperdilated, show signs of vessel dysfunction, and haemorrhage may occur (Bergers and Song, 2005).
evidence: The claim cites Kamouchi et al., 2012 as the source for pericyte sensitivity to hypoxia.

claim: When vessels lose or develop abnormal pericytes they become hyperdilated, show signs of vessel dysfunction, and haemorrhage may occur.
source: Pericytes are highly sensitive to hypoxia (Kamouchi et al., 2012), especially in brain and retina where they are most abundant, and when vessels lose or develop abnormal pericytes they become hyperdilated, show signs of vessel dysfunction, and haemorrhage may occur (Bergers and Song, 2005).
evidence: The claim cites Bergers and Song, 2005 as the source for the consequences of pericyte loss.

claim: Retina and brain present similar pathological features in CM, including haemorrhages.
source: The retina and brain present similar pathological features in CM, including haemorrhages (Greiner et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim cites Greiner et al., 2015 as the source for the similarity between retinal and brain pathology.

claim: Retina and brain may have similar dysfunction/loss of pericytes in fatal paediatric CM.
source: These data suggest that retina and brain may have similar dysfunction/loss of pericytes in fatal paediatric CM.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on unpublished brain data showing similar pericyte changes to those found in the retina.

claim: Neuroglial effects of retinal sequestration are likely to be widespread and include disturbance of tight junction regulation causing BRB/BBB breakdown with vasogenic oedema.
source: These neuroglial effects of retinal sequestration are likely to be widespread and include disturbance of tight junction regulation causing BRB/BBB breakdown with vasogenic oedema, an implicated pathway for brain swelling and death (Taylor et al., 2004; Mohanty et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the observed glial activation and cites Taylor et al., 2004 and Mohanty et al., 2017 for the pathway to brain swelling.

claim: Retinal whitening is topographically associated with capillary non-perfusion and is found in watershed zones of the retina, sites of high metabolic demand.
source: We have previously shown that retinal whitening is topographically associated with capillary non-perfusion and is found in watershed zones of the retina, sites of high metabolic demand (Beare et al., 2009), suggesting that tissue hypoxia is a principal pathogenic pathway (White et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim cites Beare et al., 2009 as the source for the topographical association between whitening and non-perfusion.

claim: Ganglion cells showed increased expression of VEGFR1, which, in combination with VEGF, is neuroprotective during ischaemia.
source: Ganglion cells showed increased expression of VEGFR1, which, in combination with VEGF, is neuroprotective during ischaemia (Saint-Geniez et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim cites Saint-Geniez et al., 2008 as the source for the neuroprotective role of VEGFR1.

claim: AQP4 is a water channel protein linked to hypoxic oncotic swelling.
source: Glia in retinal zones where whitening is mainly localised were found to express AQP4, a water channel protein linked to hypoxic oncotic swelling.
evidence: The claim draws on established knowledge about the function of AQP4.

claim: The findings support inner retinal neuronal ischaemia as opposed to dysfunction of the outer retinal photoreceptors and choroidal circulation.
source: This all supports inner retinal neuronal ischaemia as opposed to dysfunction of the outer retinal photoreceptors and choroidal circulation.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the localization of VEGFR1 and AQP4 expression to the inner retina.

claim: Orange vessels can be seen clinically with the indirect and direct ophthalmoscope through a dilated pupil by a trained physician.
source: Orange vessels can be seen clinically with the indirect and direct ophthalmoscope through a dilated pupil by a trained physician (Taylor et al., 2004), but these skills are mainly available in research or tertiary centres in malaria endemic areas (Swamy et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim cites Taylor et al., 2004 and Swamy et al., 2018 regarding the clinical detection of orange vessels and availability of expertise.

claim: There is good evidence that the clinicopathological features of CM in the retina parallel those seen in the brain.
source: There is good evidence that the clinicopathological features of CM in the retina parallel those seen in the brain (Barrera et al., 2015; MacCormick et al., 2014): ring-shaped haemorrhages (White et al., 2009; Dorovini-Zis et al., 2011), pathology of sequestration, associations between retinal features and that key neurological pathways seem to be non-functioning ('pathways to neural cell death').
evidence: The claim cites multiple studies (Barrera et al., 2015; MacCormick et al., 2014; White et al., 2009; Dorovini-Zis et al., 2011) supporting the parallel between retinal and brain pathology.

claim: Including children without MR in clinical trials is likely to reduce their power to detect an effect of an intervention on CM outcomes.
source: It should be recognised that including children without MR in clinical trials is likely to reduce their power to detect an effect of an intervention on CM outcomes.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the finding that MR increases diagnostic specificity for CM.
